text:
### Observed differences

- The branch A32–A33–A38 disappeared. In the earlier window each of A32, A33 and A38 ran in about 49 in 100 traces, and each pair of them co-occurred in about 48–49 in 100, indicating one shared branch; in the later window each appears in only about 1 of 200 traces and no pair co-occurs. [OCC005, OCC006, OCC007, REL028, REL029, REL030]
- A27 became near-universal. It ran in about 52 in 100 traces before versus about 199 in 200 after (once per trace). Before, A27 and the A32/A33/A38 branch were mutually exclusive alternatives (co-occurrence near zero, each side about half the traces); after, A27 is present in almost every trace while the branch is gone. [OCC004, REL022, REL023, REL024]
- Routing after A26 collapsed onto a single successor. Before, A26's observed outgoing transitions split roughly 50 in 100 to A27, 18 to A38, 16 to A33 and 14 to A32; after, about 98 in 100 lead to A27. A27 now co-occurs with A14, A15 and A26 in about 99.5 in 100 traces (previously about half), and A28 now follows A27 in about 96 in 100 traces, whereas before A28 followed the A32/A33/A38 side (co-occurrence about 48.5 in 100). [DIR006, REL009, REL013, REL017, REL021, REL025, REL026, REL027]
- A04 receded from the main flow. It ran in about 68 in 100 traces before versus about 22 in 100 after; before, A14 was followed by A04 in about 63 of its observed outgoing transitions (A15 about 36), after A14 leads mostly to A15 (about 82) and rarely to A04 (about 10). A04 also stopped preceding A26 and A28 (about 62–64 in 100 before, about 12–13 after) and now appears later in the trace (mean relative position about 0.21 versus 0.40). [OCC002, DIR002, DIR004, REL001, REL003, REL005, POS001]
- A02 and A08 occur more often (about 5 to 15 and 5 to 20 in 100 traces, respectively) with substantially changed successor profiles; these rest on only about 10–40 observations per window and are weak. [OCC001, OCC003, DIR001, DIR003]
- The core A15 → A16 succession is essentially stable (about 98 in 100 of A15's outgoing transitions before, about 92 after). [DIR005]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports a structural change in which the alternative branch A32 → A33 → A38 between A26 and A28 is no longer executed. In the earlier window, A26 routed about half of its outgoing transitions to A27 and about half into the A32/A33/A38 branch, with both routes converging on A28; in the later window, A26 leads to A27 in about 98 in 100 of its outgoing transitions, A27 precedes A28 in about 96–97 in 100 traces, and A32, A33 and A38 each appear in only about 1 of 200 traces. Because the branch activities are nearly absent in the later window, this points to a path being removed (or effectively no longer exercised) rather than a re-weighting between paths that both remain in use. The screening context supports this reading: 52 control-flow items qualified where about 0.65 would be expected if nothing had changed, so chance re-sampling cannot account for the pattern as a whole. Limitations: the later-window profiles of A32, A33 and A38 rest on a single trace each, and the evidence cannot rule out that the branch still exists for a share of cases too small to appear in the 200 later traces, so removal and extreme rarefaction cannot be distinguished. [OCC004, OCC005, OCC006, OCC007, DIR006, REL017, REL021, REL022, REL023, REL024, REL028, REL029, REL030]

Other differences:
- A04 largely dropped out of the flow between A14 and A15: before, A14 led to A04 in about 63 of its observed outgoing transitions and A04 preceded A26 and A28 in most traces containing them; after, A14 leads mainly to A15, A04 appears in about 22 in 100 traces, and it sits later in the trace (mean relative position about 0.21 versus 0.40). The evidence cannot show whether this is connected to the branch removal or an independent change. [OCC002, DIR002, DIR004, REL001, REL002, REL003, REL005, POS001]
- A02 and A08 are observed more often with substantially changed successors, but on few observations in each window. [OCC001, OCC003, DIR001, DIR003]
